hypothesis: RUNTIME surface: decouple the crystal-synth claims_zh tail budget from `auto_max_per_run`. That field means 'max SOURCES daily auto-enqueues per run' (default 30); bilingual_tail-v1 reused it as the claims-translation attempts cap, so a synth that adds 100+ claims can only translate 30 per run and — with no other automatic trigger — the backlog never converges (production vault 2026-08: exactly 30 translated, 105 stranded). v2 adds `auto_claim_zh_max_per_run` (serde default 0 = unlimited) to `.ovp/source-work.toml` and points ONLY the claims tail at it; the batch's consecutive-failure breaker (MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS = 3) already contains provider outages. v2 also appends one JSON line per tail run to `.ovp/crystal/claims_zh_runs.jsonl` (schema/model/translated/skipped/errors/remaining) because tail results previously existed only on stdout and were unrecoverable after unattended runs. Predicted: a claims backlog drains in one synth run instead of never; zh coverage tracks the EN authority; every tail run leaves an auditable record.

predicted_delta.operational_reliability: claims_zh backlog converges to 0 in a single run regardless of size, instead of being throttled to the daily enqueue budget forever; `claims_zh_runs.jsonl` makes remaining-backlog regressions diagnosable after the fact
predicted_delta.coverage: portal zh claim coverage tracks the EN authority within one run even after large synth batches (the 105-claim production hole would have closed in the same run)

guardrails.en_authority_untouched: unchanged from v1 — the tail writes only the rebuildable projection `.ovp/crystal/claims_zh.json` plus the NEW append-only log `.ovp/crystal/claims_zh_runs.jsonl`; the crystal ledger is read, never written
guardrails.legacy_config_compatible: a source-work.toml without `auto_claim_zh_max_per_run` loads with 0 = unlimited, so existing vaults get backlog-draining behavior without operator action; setting the field restores capping
guardrails.cards_and_theme_pages_unchanged: cards_zh_tail (daily) and theme_pages_zh_tail keep the v1 `auto_max_per_run` cap — this candidate touches the claims tail only
guardrails.outage_containment: uncapped runs are still bounded by translate_claims_batch's MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS breaker: a provider outage aborts after 3 consecutive paid failures instead of retrying the whole backlog
guardrails.failure_isolation: every tail failure including the run-log append degrades to a warn line; the parent run's exit code is still decided by the EN phases alone
guardrails.replay_mode_no_calls: unchanged from v1 — replay/offline runs skip the tail before any client, config, or log work (no claims_zh.json, no claims_zh_runs.jsonl)

eval_plan.replay_set: ovp-cli tests on temp vaults with a stub ModelClient: (1) auto_max_per_run=1 + auto_claim_zh_max_per_run unset (0) → the tail translates the FULL missing backlog in one run and the run log records remaining=0; (2) positive claims cap → attempts bounded, run log records the true remaining backlog; (3) follow-up unlimited run drains the rest and APPENDS a second record (log is append-only); (4) pre-field source-work.toml loads with the cap defaulting to unlimited; (5) existing gate tests (replay skip / flag off / malformed config) still pass and additionally assert no run-log file appears

rollback: Set `auto_claim_zh_max_per_run = 30` (or any positive cap) in `.ovp/source-work.toml` to restore v1 throttling without a code change. Code rollback is a single revert: the changes are the new config field, the claims tail's budget source, the run-log append, and one stdout field.
